decisions.topic: How a step's dependencies on an earlier-step answer reach the form
decisions.choice: At parse time in useTemplateSchema, a new pure helper liftCrossStepDependencies in lib/schema.ts rewrites each dependencies entry whose trigger key is not in the step's own properties into an equivalent allOf if/then entry; the rewritten schema feeds both mergedSchema and extractSchemaFromStep.
rejected: Injecting hidden stub properties for earlier-step keys into the step schema
Resolving every condition ourselves with retrieveSchema before handing the schema to rjsf
Changing Stepper.tsx to pass a merged multi-step schema to the Form
decisions.reason: rjsf skips a dependency whose trigger is not in the step's properties, while if/then is already evaluated against the whole formData (stepsState); lifting only those skipped entries fixes cross-step dependencies without changing same-step behaviour.

decisions.choice: Only entries where the step schema has a properties object and the dependency key is not an own key of it; steps without properties, same-step dependencies and boolean dependency values stay untouched.
rejected: Lift only when the key is defined in an earlier step
decisions.reason: This is exactly the set rjsf silently skips today, so no template that works today changes, and the existing useTemplateSchema test for a step with dependencies and no properties keeps passing.

decisions.choice: Array dependency D on key k becomes {if: {required: [k]}, then: {required: D}}; schema dependency S without oneOf becomes {if: {required: [k]}, then: S}; schema dependency with oneOf becomes one {if: {properties: {k: branch.properties[k]}, required: [k]}, then: branch without properties[k]} per branch that defines properties[k], plus {if: {required: [k]}, then: rest} when the dependency has keys besides oneOf.
decisions.reason: Matches rjsf and JSON Schema dependency semantics (applies when the trigger has an answer; a oneOf branch applies when its trigger subschema matches) using keywords both rjsf and json-schema-library already resolve against data.

decisions.choice: No change to Stepper.tsx, createAsyncValidators.ts, Workflow or any file in plugins/scaffolder.
decisions.reason: The Form already receives formData={stepsState} and handleNext validates the full submitted formData, so with the lifted schema both rjsf and createAsyncValidators resolve conditions against all earlier answers; TemplateWizardPage and TemplateEditorForm render the shared Workflow/Stepper (FR-10).

decisions.choice: findSchemaForKey resolves each step's mergedSchema with getSchema against the full form state minus the looked-up key; a key found in no step but declared in some step's conditional branch (isKeyDeclaredInSchemas) is dropped from Review; a key declared nowhere is still listed under formatKey(key).
rejected: Keep passing only the dependency keys as data
Pass the full form state including the key
decisions.reason: Removing the key itself stops json-schema-library from inventing a schema from the value, while every other answer (same step or earlier step) drives if/then/else, allOf and dependencies, so active branch fields get their title and review options and inactive ones disappear.

decisions.topic: Values of fields whose condition stopped holding
decisions.choice: Dropped from the Review step only; onCreate still receives them unchanged.

units.behaviour: Adds liftCrossStepDependencies, a pure helper that rewrites a step's dependencies keyed on a property the step does not define (an earlier-step answer) into equivalent allOf if/then entries, so rjsf and json-schema-library evaluate them against the whole wizard form data.
rules: 1. Signature: export const liftCrossStepDependencies = (schema: JsonObject): JsonObject; it never mutates its input or any nested object of it (build new objects with spread).
2. If schema.dependencies is not an object (use the file's isObject guard) or schema.properties is not an object, return the input schema itself (same reference).
3. Walk Object.entries(schema.dependencies) in order. An entry whose key is an own key of schema.properties (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call) stays in the remaining dependencies untouched.
4. For any other key k: an array value D becomes one lifted entry { if: { required: [k] }, then: { required: D } }.
5. For any other key k: an object value without an array oneOf becomes one lifted entry { if: { required: [k] }, then: <the dependency value> }.

6. For any other key k: an object value with an array oneOf becomes, for each oneOf branch that is an object whose properties object has own key k, one entry { if: { properties: { [k]: branch.properties[k] }, required: [k] }, then: <branch copy whose properties omit k> }; branches without k are skipped; if the dependency value has keys other than oneOf, add one more entry { if: { required: [k] }, then: <those other keys> } after the branch entries.
7. Any other value type (boolean, string) for key k stays in the remaining dependencies untouched.
8. If nothing was lifted, return the input schema itself (same reference).

9. Otherwise return { ...schema, allOf: [...existing schema.allOf entries when schema.allOf is an array, ...lifted entries in walk order] } with dependencies set to the remaining entries, and with the dependencies key removed entirely when none remain.

10. Put it after extractSchemaFromStep, with a TSDoc comment explaining that rjsf skips dependencies whose trigger is not one of the step's own properties; give it no release tag and do not add it to lib/index.ts (it stays internal).

units.behaviour: findSchemaForKey resolves each step schema against every other answer of the form, and a new isKeyDeclaredInSchemas reports whether a key is defined anywhere in a step schema, including inactive conditional branches.
rules: 1. findSchemaForKey keeps its name, parameters and return type; for each step in order it builds data as a copy of formState without the looked-up key (lodash omit) and calls new JSONSchema(step.mergedSchema).getSchema({ pointer: `#/${key}`, data }).
2. A step matches only when the result is truthy and not a JsonError (isJsonError from json-schema-library); return the first matching step, else null.

3. Replace the old block comment with one explaining why the key itself is left out of data (json-schema-library would otherwise invent a schema from its value) while all other answers, from this or earlier steps, drive if/then/else, allOf and dependencies.
4. Add export function isKeyDeclaredInSchemas(key: string, schemas: ParsedTemplateSchema[]): boolean, true when any step's mergedSchema declares key.

5. A schema node declares key when it is a JSON object (isJsonObject) whose properties object has own key key, or when any entry of its allOf, anyOf or oneOf arrays, its then or else, or any value of its dependencies object declares key (recursive; do not descend into nested properties or items).
6. Keep isJsonObject and formatKey unchanged.
